messages:
Sam: got alert ~20m ago: increase in 504/502 for eu-west inference endpoints. traffic supposed to fail to eu-west2 but many clients kept hitting old ips.
Li: confirmed eu-west1 gpu pool drained for maintenance. reserved fallback to eu-west2 kicked in, but latency + 5xx spiked for some customers.
devops-bot: action: dns-update applied by Sam at 1719013340 — set weight(eu-west1)=0 -> weight(eu-west2)=1; attempted ttl change 300->60
Marta: were TTLs lowered *before* the weight flip? if not we might be stuck with cached records for a while.
Sam: we pushed TTL=60 then flipped weights. thought that order was fine; looks like many resolvers still returning old 300s.
Li: sampling from public resolvers:
```
# 8.8.8.8
api.redwood-eu.company.com.  230  IN A  35.194.12.77
# 1.1.1.1
api.redwood-eu.company.com.  298  IN A  35.194.12.77
# customer-isp
api.redwood-eu.company.com.  1500 IN A  35.194.12.77  <-- stale cache
```
Li: some corporate/ISP resolvers ignore decreases in TTL or apply minimum caching windows. EDNS subnet differences causing region-specific divergence.
AJ: app-side mitigation idea: have SDKs retry on 503 with an alternate host header or 302 to eu-west2. may break clients though.
Marta: options we discussed:
- withdraw old IP via BGP (fast) — requires carrier ops coordination
- create CNAME -> global LB we control and can reconfigure quickly (but caches still a risk)
- have apps use service discovery / metadata for region endpoints
Sam: nginx frontends can add X-Fallback-Host header to help smart SDKs retry. but older SDKs won't use it.
Networking: if resolvers keep returning old A records, withdrawing the IP from BGP will drop it and force the world to re-resolve (most clients will then get new IP).
Li: warning: BGP withdraw causes a hard disconnect for any clients actively using the old ip; need to ensure eu-west2 LB ready and warm.
Sam: also cost concern — cross-region egress from eu-west2 to eu-west1 is higher; if failover persists we'll incur extra egress. finance needs a heads-up if >1h.
devops-bot: created task INCD-4827: DNS propagation troubleshooting + TTL handbook update.
Marta: immediate playbook:
1) push authoritative TTL=30 across prod-eu zones where safe
2) coordinate BGP withdraw of old eu-west1 LB IPs with carrier ops
3) enable X-Fallback-Host header on frontends and ship SDK hotfix to use it
4) update failover runbook: lower TTL >=30m before planned flips, warm GPU pools in target region
Sam: command snippet used for Cloud DNS swap:
```
gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=prod-eu
# remove old
gcloud dns record-sets transaction remove --name=api.redwood-eu.company.com. --ttl=300 --type=A 35.194.12.77 --zone=prod-eu
# add with lower ttl
gcloud dns record-sets transaction add --name=api.redwood-eu.company.com. --ttl=60 --type=A 34.89.22.10 --zone=prod-eu
gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute --zone=prod-eu
```
Li: note: lowering TTL isn't guaranteed: some ISPs ignore sub-60s or enforce min-cache windows; treat DNS as eventually consistent.
AJ: i'll start the SDK branch for exponential retry + alternate-host header. target hotfix in 2h.
Networking: coordinating BGP withdraw in 10m with carrier ops. will mark exact withdraw+reannounce times here before action.
oncall-bot: bridge: incident-eu-dns-1719013478 scheduled — joining...
Marta: after stabilization we'll run a post-incident: owners @Sam @Li @AJ. include cost impact, TTL guidance, GPU pool pre-warm checklist.
Sam: executing BGP withdraw at 1719013520 unless objections. will monitor 5xx rate and token-latency traces.
Li: after partial withdraw we saw majority traffic flip within ~30s, error rate dropped from ~10% -> ~1.2%. watching for cold starts on large model pools.
AJ: notified CS and two impacted customers via cs-notify.
Sam: BGP withdraw completed at 1719013525. residual traffic for ~20-40s, then normal. starting follow-ups: TTL hardening, SDK fallback, cost sign-off.
Marta: logged follow-ups and assigned postmortem. good job everyone :thumbsup:
